criteria.justification: The response explicitly contrasts the “real cost” of changing the public commitment with the “deeper loss of trust” from failing the audience’s top credibility test. It specifically uses both the workshop ranking and the commentator’s track record, appropriately treating the latter as a warning and practitioner evidence as stronger.

It emphasizes that the skip-level director “already rejected an even narrower release for the same underlying concern” and concludes that another reduced-scope version cannot be treated as implicitly approved.

The response acknowledges and owns the cost of changing the public commitment but recommends delaying because the product’s core estimation claim remains indefensible, using the conference for honest engagement instead.

It considers reduced scope through a separately approved research preview or limited pilot and notes the prior rejection of an even narrower release. However, it does not directly evaluate whether any launch limited to existing transaction types could meet defensible precision and recall thresholds; it mainly concludes the currently described subset has low recall.

It provides a concrete plan: escalate a decision memo within days, define evidence-based launch gates, time-box feasibility and evaluation work, test a limited pilot, and promptly reset expectations with customers, partners, and conference stakeholders.
